forbiddenRegisterNote: N-233 (6.0 section 3.9, C-19) — the Game Guide's forbidden register: the combat skin.
The Game Guide edition is a vocabulary for a life, not a genre. Swords, health bars,
enemies, damage and boss fights import a frame in which a person has hit points, other
people are obstacles, and a hard year is a fight somebody lost. Each of those is the
worth score coming back in through the register — the one channel the no-score wall,
which governs words, numbers and totals, never reached.
TWO SCOPES, because the words are not all of one kind.
forbiddenRegister is the whole list and it governs the EDITION VOCABULARY: no Game
Guide label and no first-use gloss in content/terminology.ts may contain any of these,
whatever else the word might mean. Choosing 'damage' or 'boss' as the game word for
something is choosing the frame, and that is the choice this list forbids.
forbiddenRegisterPlaySurfaces is the subset that is ALSO linted over every string the
play surfaces render. It is smaller on purpose. 'damage', 'kill', 'boss' and 'grind'
are ordinary English before they are game words — the shipped pool contains 'one
constraint was doing all the damage', 'Kill the most expensive first' (the debt
avalanche, by its usual name), 'what actually killed it' and 'grind it out', none of
which is a combat skin and none of which 6.0 may rewrite. A lint that fired on those
would be pushed to fire less, and a lint under that pressure stops meaning anything.
So the subset holds only terms that cannot be anything but the skin, and the wider
list holds the line where the frame is actually chosen: in the edition's own words.
Proven red by planting 'health bar' into a game label.
